friends saddened by their loss. bishop michael router at father hegarty’s rock only three weeks after his installation as bishop of derry, the most rev erend michael router paid a pastoral visit last sunday to the parishes of burt, inch & fahan and desertegney & lower fahan (buncrana). we were delighted to have him amongst us on what was an unse asonably warm and sunny day, for what was a spectacularly wonderful occasion. he walked with us on a synodal walk from the stone jug and celebrated mass on father hegarty’s rock, before returning then to cockhill parish hall for tea and refreshments. the turnout was splendid, the welcome warm, the support immense and faith tangible. in the midst of a sometimes stiff atlantic breeze he joked about not being blown into the water, seemingly perched as he was on the edge of the lough. but from there he commanded a great view of the gathering and the statue of friar seamus hegarty op – and he offered a most memorable mass recalling the courage and hope which father hegarty had in abundance, and asking god to grant us the same gifts for the challenges in our own time. the music and si nging were outstanding and the joy and contentment of those gathered there, of all ages, was clear to be seen. after visiting father walsh in his home, the bishop returned to derry with a s pring in his step and firm in the knowledge that he will always be welcome in these parts. it was a truly wonderful occasion made possible only by the devotion and help of huge teams of people: o ur stewards and volunteers, choirs and musicians, farmers and bakers, schools and parents’ associations (especially at st oran’s ns), and to all who came to celebrate. to them all and to god himself, we mus t always be thankful. father bradley please note there will be no 7pm mass on wednesday 21st october and no 10am mass on friday 23rd october in st mura’s parish church, fahan throwing open the doors to christ novena this year’s novena begins next sunday 25 october at 7pm in st mary’s church, cockhill. for the nine sundays before christmas we will gather for one hour and the ceremony will comprise of the rosary, a talk given by an invited speaker, the novena prayer and pe titions (which can be placed in a box at the door of the church), a eucharistic healing ceremony and fini shing with benediction of the most blessed sacrament. once again, the theme of this year’s novena is “throwing open the doors to christ ” – taken from the homily of pope st john paul at the opening mass of his pontificate on 22 october 1978. the first gues t speaker on the opening night will be bishop michael router. all are very welcome. please come along, bring your families and make the most of this opportunity for prayer as we approach the season of chris t’s birth. (the holy hour each sunday evening in st mary’s oratory will cease for the moment, resuming after christmas.) prayer for vocations st paul could have written this passage from today's second reading to our se minarians and to the men discerning their vocation: "we know, brothers, that god loves you and that have been chosen, because when we brought the good news to you, it came to you not only as words, but a s power and the holy spirit and as utter conviction." fahan
